source.title: Training, Reading, and Editing Legible Transformers

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and polysemanticity and reports results on its own legible-by-construction models, but it does not test whether ordinary neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether those mixtures are caused by superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper measures detection, category decoding, and distribution of computations in bounded units of its own architecture. Those results are relevant to unit legibility and localization, but do not measure polysemanticity as defined in the claim versions. Background statements and results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds a custom bounded-operator transformer and measures selectivity (crisp and contextual), vocabulary decodability, causal rank of blocks, edit locality and circuit fan-in/fan-out. None of these counts how many units respond to unrelated inputs or contexts, so no version's effect is measured. Superposition and polysemanticity appear only as framing. The paper says the GELU model spreads a prediction over a 'cloud of polysemantic units', but it measures only attribution spread, not polysemanticity. SoLU is cited, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a variance-floor objective makes bounded operators crisp and alive at parity quality, and that detection and naming dissociate. The model still distributes abstract, nameless concepts, which they liken to superposition in ordinary networks. Decorrelation trades reuse for editability rather than raising per-unit legibility.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a legible-by-construction transformer with bounded fuzzy set operators, variance-floor and decorrelation objectives, then measures unit detection, decoding, and circuit structure. It does not apply the original sources' method for identifying polysemantic neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported selective fraction is sensitive to the variance threshold and checkpoint because many channels sit near the cutoff. Decodability also changes with readout: raw logit-lens decoding is 38.7%, while decoding in either raw or unit-specific tuned frames is 65.3%.

fits_no_version.finding: Detection is more common than naming: 78% of operands are selective, 38.7% are raw-decodable, and 65.3% decode in either frame.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In bounded legible transformer units, input-dependent detection and vocabulary naming dissociate, and tuned readout raises nameability.

fits_no_version.finding: Token-level features are localized to single units; late-layer abstract computations need rank about 256 to reconstruct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this constructed transformer, token features are single-unit while abstract concepts are distributed more with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Decorrelation lowers operand correlation and reshapes fan-out into fan-in without raising the selective fraction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Between-unit decorrelation changes circuit shape and editability but not per-unit selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct logit attribution for 'than' spreads over about 1200 contributors in a GELU model, versus about 15 in the decorrelated bounded model and about 31 in the baseline bounded model. No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bounded legible units concentrate per-prediction attribution relative to conventional GELU MLPs.

record.problems: All results are single seed at this scale. The reported units are from a custom bounded-operator architecture, not conventional transformer MLP neurons; detection, decodability, and selectivity are not direct measures of polysemanticity. The paper notes that the selective-count threshold is fragile near its variance cutoff.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were omitted. Background claims and findings attributed to cited work were excluded.

untested.parts: No count of conventional MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts; the GELU baseline is used only for edit collateral and attribution spread.
No feature-count versus capacity manipulation. Distributed abstract concepts are only interpreted as compatible with superposition.
Architecture and decorrelation are varied, but the share of polysemantic units is never measured; selectivity is not monosemanticity.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not revisited.
Threshold and readout sensitivity concerns selectivity and decodability, not polysemanticity classification.

record.verdict_notes: All results are single seed at 125M scale. The 'polysemantic' wording about the GELU baseline is interpretive and has no polysemanticity measurement behind it. The edit-locality results (184x and 52x, about 410x overall versus GELU) are also not about polysemanticity.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision neuron is studied.

The study does not measure whether MLP neurons in language models respond to unrelated tokens or contexts. Its layerwise measurements concern selectivity and category decoding in bounded operators of its own architecture.
The paper does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons, or compare feature load with neuron capacity.
It does not test whether polysemanticity arises from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
The paper varies architecture and training pressures, but reports legibility and circuit organization rather than the share of polysemantic neurons or its reduction.
The study does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons to determine whether their mixed inputs share a feature or related function.
It reports sensitivity of its selectivity and decodability measures, but does not test how activation range or explanation scoring changes a polysemanticity classification.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Measured feed-forward operand selectivity on held-out text; selective means crisp and contextual under the stated thresholds.
rows.note: Selectivity is a detector-legibility measure, not a measure of unrelated input meanings.

rows.note: This measures category decoding, not whether a unit responds to unrelated inputs.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed a single intersection unit's write and measured the loss change.
rows.note: The paper says single-unit ablation cannot distinguish redundant copies from a distributed code.
rows.check: Baseline is listed as 'not stated', but the text gives whole intersection-block ablation at 0.65 nats as the contrast. The state should not read 'observed' when no version-linked effect exists.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Ablated an intersection block and added back a rank-4 reconstruction of its residual contribution.
rows.measure: Share of block ablation effect restored
rows.note: The authors interpret the early-layer block as a few operators replicated across many units.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Ablated an intersection block and reconstructed its residual contribution at increasing rank.
rows.measure: Rank needed for reconstruction to restore the block's effect
rows.note: The authors interpret the late-layer computation as distributed across units.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Compared the best individual intersection unit with the whole block's best linear combination on held-out token categories.
rows.measure: Held-out detection AUC; best single unit versus whole block
rows.note: This is a token-level detection task, not a test of unrelated meanings.

rows.subject: annealed model
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of selective feed-forward operands under a between-unit decorrelation training pressure.
rows.note: The paper reports this measure as averaged over 200k/250k/end-of-epoch checkpoints to address threshold fluctuation.

rows.subject: decorrelated model (λd=1)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of selective feed-forward operands under a between-unit decorrelation training pressure.
rows.note: The paper says per-unit legibility is lower than the baseline and does not rise monotonically with the decorrelation pressure.
rows.check: 'Partial' implies a version-relative effect; the row bears on no version. The selective fraction is non-monotone across λd (51.6% at 3e-1).
